title: heap-buffer-overflow in _io__RawIOBase_read
consumer: not established; the trigger is the upstream fix's own regression test
live_proof: measured, not asserted: the trigger runs on the pinned 3.13.7 ASan build (PYTHONMALLOC=malloc, ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=0) and reports ASAN:heap-buffer-overflow in a 8193-byte region. Running it is the liveness proof -- a sanitizer report here means the defect is present in this tree.
fidelity: the trigger is upstream's own reproducer from the issue, run through the real interpreter rather than reduced to a C model. What it does NOT establish is which arm ought to catch it.
allocator_layer: libc malloc (the object never reaches a pymalloc pool)
layer_note: measured: ASan reported a 8193-byte region, over the 512 B SMALL_REQUEST_THRESHOLD

cheribsd-revocation.oracle: the arm does not separate this case, and the admissible outcomes are stated rather than one of them predicted: si_code=1 (PROT_CHERI_BOUNDS) where the access goes beyond the bounds the allocator actually set, si_code=2 (PROT_CHERI_TAG) where it instead lands in memory a revocation sweep has already reclaimed, or completion where it stays inside the bounds the allocator set -- malloc may bound a capability to a rounded size class rather than the requested length. The mechanism is live and the run proves it rather than assuming it: mech-control S_OOB faults with si_code=1. Any other si_code would falsify this.
cheribsd-revocation.verdict_note: DETECTED si_code=2 (PROT_CHERI_TAG). The code is the tag rule, the mechanism is the bounds rule: see note (3). Re-measured 2026-10-19 with ONLY=08 bash probe/run-cheribsd.sh.

status: measured on three arms; matrix rows in results/20261006/matrix.tsv: spatial DETECTED cause=5 (spatial-20261008-033909); sublet DETECTED cause=5 (sublet-20261008-034649); cheribsd-revocation DETECTED si_code=2 (cheri11)
fault_sites_why: Host ASan (CPython 3.13.7 --with-address-sanitizer, PYTHONMALLOC=malloc, results/2026-10-10-asan/sites.tsv) reports heap-buffer-overflow (READ 1048576) at memcpy ../../../../src/libsanitizer/sanitizer_common/sanitizer_common_interceptors_memintrinsics.inc:117 | memcpy /usr/include/x86_64-linux-gnu/bits/string_fortified.h:29 | PyBytes_FromStringAndSize Objects/bytesobject.c:159. That run uses no Capstone arm and was recorded before any virtual arm ran.
note: (1) All three arms detect this defect. The Capstone arms fault cause=28 on `lbu a4, 0x0(a1)` in memcpy, the copy itself crossing the bound. Spatial, NON-NESTED -- the ASan heap report survives PYTHONMALLOC=pymalloc, so the object is libc malloc's. (2) The 2026-10-18 review withdrew the CheriBSD cell for reporting si_code=2 instead of si_code=1. That withdrawal is RETRACTED. Its stated reason -- 'malloc rounds the request up to a size class, so the overread stays inside the capability' -- was case 01's reasoning and does not fit: ASan records READ 1048576 out of an 8193-byte region and no rounding absorbs a megabyte. (3) Measured in the guest, varying only the length readinto claims and changing nothing else. tools/cheribsd/capbounds first measures the source block: malloc(8193) returns a capability of length 10240. Then: 10000 and 10240 do not fault at all; 10241, 11000, 12288, 16384 and 24576 fault si_code=1 PROT_CHERI_BOUNDS at si_addr=0x40ba4afa; 32768, 49152, 65536 and 1048576 fault si_code=2 PROT_CHERI_TAG at si_addr=0x40ba4b70. Three readings follow. 10240 is the last length that does not fault, so the rounding blind spot here is 2047 bytes. Every fault lands at one of two fixed addresses 118 bytes apart, so the copy is stopped at the object's edge whatever is claimed -- at a megabyte it does not run a megabyte. And the code flips between 24576 and 32768, exactly where capbounds independently finds this block's tag going (+16384 keeps it, +32768 loses it): beyond the representable range of a compressed 128-bit capability the pointer arithmetic clears the tag, so the same rejection is reported under the tag code. (4) The general rule this corrects: a capability system has three regimes, not two -- inside the rounded bound nothing is seen, past it the bounds check fires, far past it the tag rule fires. 'Spatial defect implies si_code=1' is a proxy that holds for small overshoots only. The other si_code=2 withdrawals (01, 05, 09, 10) are small-overshoot cells where the question is whether the access succeeded, and it did.
